scriptVersion: Remake v2.1 (Retention Playbook; fact-check round 3 fixes applied)

claims.statement: HOOK: Fifty million dollars. That was the price tag on Netflix. And Blockbuster said no.
claims.evidence: All three accounts name $50M (Antioco LinkedIn Dec 2021; Hastings via Marketplace 2020; Randolph memoir). No deal happened. No 'laughed' in the hook.

claims.statement: PROMISE: Today, Netflix is worth hundreds of billions.
claims.evidence: Market cap ~$293B (mid-Oct 2026) and up; conservative wording (round 2).

claims.statement: Down to one store. In Oregon. / A single franchised store. In Bend, Oregon.
claims.evidence: Wikipedia: only one franchised store remains open, in Bend, Oregon.

claims.statement: PROMISE: And the boardroom fight, seven years later, that most retellings skip.
claims.evidence: FIXED (round 3 issue 4). 2000 to 2007 = seven years (8-K 19 Mar 2007; FY2006 release 27 Feb 2007). 'Most retellings skip' is a hedged framing line, no longer an absolute claim.

claims.statement: Dallas, Texas. Blockbuster headquarters. The year is two thousand.
claims.evidence: All accounts agree on a meeting at Blockbuster's Dallas HQ; year 2000 is the safe wording (c14 disputed month).

claims.statement: Blockbuster was born right here in Dallas, in nineteen eighty-five.
claims.evidence: Wikipedia: first store opened 19 Oct 1985 in Dallas.

claims.statement: Thousands of stores. Close to five billion dollars a year in revenue. Up about eleven percent.
John Antioco. Around twenty years at Seven-Eleven. Then Circle K. Then Taco Bell. In 1997, the top job at Blockbuster.
claims.evidence: Verified rounds 2-3 (Wikipedia: June 1997, Taco Bell president Antioco became Blockbuster CEO).

claims.statement: In the building: three visitors from California. Reed Hastings and Marc Randolph... And their finance chief, Barry McCarthy.
claims.evidence: FIXED (round 3 issue 5). 'In the building' no longer seats Antioco at the pitch, so it is compatible with all three accounts (Antioco says he only greeted the guests). Visitors per Randolph's memoir.

claims.statement: Reed Hastings and Marc Randolph, who founded Netflix in 1997.
claims.evidence: Prospectus: incorporated in Delaware in August 1997.

claims.statement: Since September 1999, one flat monthly fee.
claims.evidence: Prospectus: subscription service launched in September 1999.

claims.statement: About twenty-five million American homes will own a player. Nearly double. Twenty-one billion dollars renting and buying videos.
claims.evidence: Prospectus citing Adams Media: ~25M US households end 2001 (+91%); $21B video rentals and purchases in 2001.

claims.statement: About three hundred thousand subscribers. Revenue $35.9M. Loss $57.4M.
claims.evidence: Prospectus: 2000 revenue $35,894K, net loss $57,363K; ~292,000 subscribers end 2000.

claims.statement: Every version agrees on that number. Almost everything else is disputed. Who was in the room. What was said. Even the month.
claims.evidence: $50M in all accounts; date disputed (early 2000 vs September 2000).

claims.statement: Netflix is on its way to losing more this year than its own price tag.
claims.evidence: 2000 net loss $57.4M > $50M; 'on its way' avoids hindsight.

claims.statement: In two thousand, the dot-com bubble peaked and began to burst.
claims.evidence: Nasdaq peak 10 Mar 2000.

claims.statement: Blockbuster's parent company is Viacom. Could Antioco buy Netflix on his own? We simply don't know.
claims.evidence: Viacom parent 1994-2004; framed as an open question.

claims.statement: Fifty million was about one percent of Blockbuster's yearly revenue.
A rental business with no stores. No shelves. No counters. No store rent.
claims.evidence: FIXED (round 3 issue 3). Netflix had no retail outlets; it rented offices and distribution centers (prospectus), which 'no store rent' no longer denies.

claims.statement: Antioco, LinkedIn 2021: 'I can say with complete confidence that there were never any serious acquisition talks in 2000.' He wasn't even in the meeting; only stopped by to greet the guests.
claims.evidence: Verbatim match with the 23 Dec 2021 post as quoted by Stratrix; attributed.

claims.statement: In his 2019 book, That Will Never Work, he recalls Antioco struggling not to laugh.
claims.evidence: Randolph memoir excerpt (Vanity Fair, Sept 2019); framed as his recollection.

claims.statement: In 2023, he wrote on Twitter that Blockbuster 'laughed us out of the room.'
claims.evidence: Fortune, 14 Apr 2023; flagged as Randolph's memory.

claims.statement: Reed Hastings has reportedly said he doesn't think it was serious. More curiosity than anything else.
claims.evidence: Variety, 21 Mar 2025: 'I don't think it was serious. I think it was curiosity rather than anything else.' Paraphrased, hedged.

claims.statement: Three men. Three memories. Told nearly twenty years later, or more.
claims.evidence: 2019 memoir, 2020 Marketplace, 2021 LinkedIn, 2023 tweet, 2025 Variety.

claims.statement: May 2002 IPO at $15. Valued at about $310M. Six times the price tag. Offering raises $82.5M.
claims.evidence: Prospectus 22 May 2002: 5.5M shares x $15 = $82.5M; 20,648,074 shares outstanding x $15 = $309.7M (6.2x).

claims.statement: More than 600,000 subscribers. About double. More than 11,500 titles. $19.95 a month.
claims.evidence: Prospectus summary; 603k vs 292k.

claims.statement: In 2004, its peak. 9,094 stores. 84,300 employees.
claims.evidence: Wikipedia citing SEC.

claims.statement: That same year, it splits from Viacom. And launches Blockbuster Online.
claims.evidence: Spin-off Oct 2004; Blockbuster Online launched 2004.

claims.statement: January 2005. It drops most late fees.
claims.evidence: 2005 10-Q: from 1 Jan 2005 at US company-operated stores.

claims.statement: Meanwhile, a new player has arrived. Since late 2004, the activist investor Carl Icahn has been buying in. He builds a stake of nearly ten percent. In May 2005, he wins a seat on the board.
claims.evidence: FIXED (round 3 issue 2). Re-opened Schedule 13D this round: event date 14 Dec 2004; transaction table shows open-market buys from 11/11/04; 5.80% Class A / 5.07% Class B at filing, Icahn group 'holders of the largest number of outstanding shares'. Stake later near 10% and May 2005 board seat (Wikipedia; NBC May 2005). Order now correct relative to Jan 2005 late fees.

claims.statement: For 2005: a net loss of $588 million. More than half is a write-down.
claims.evidence: FY2006 release: 2005 net loss $588.1M incl. $341.9M impairment (58%).

claims.statement: Autumn 2006, Total Access. Rent online, return to a store, swap for a free rental.
claims.evidence: FY2006 release: launched ~5 months before Feb 2007; in-store exchange for free rentals.

claims.statement: About 2.2M online subscribers. 700,000 added in three months. Target 3M by end of March. Back in profit, $54.7M.
claims.evidence: FY2006 release.

claims.statement: Antioco says Netflix came back to the table. Serious talks, he says, in early 2007. That's his account.
claims.evidence: Antioco, LinkedIn Pulse 1 Jun 2022; attributed twice (single source, hedged).

claims.statement: January 2007 bonus $2.28M vs $7.65M claimed. March settlement just under five million. Old contract would have paid $13.5M.
claims.evidence: FY2006 release (25 Jan 2007, $2.28M; $7.65M); 8-K 19 Mar 2007: lump sum $4.9875M vs $13.5M under prior agreement.

claims.statement: That summer, Jim Keyes takes over as CEO.
claims.evidence: Release 2 Jul 2007.

claims.statement: That same year, Netflix starts streaming.
claims.evidence: Watch Now launched Jan 2007.

claims.statement: 23 Sept 2010 Chapter Eleven. 2011 Dish buys it, about 1,700 stores. Early 2014 last company-owned stores close.
claims.evidence: Wikipedia; last corporate stores 12 Jan 2014.

claims.statement: In 2025, revenue of $45.2B. About nine hundred times that fifty million price tag. Profit: eleven billion dollars.
claims.evidence: FIXED (round 3 issue 1). 900x now follows the revenue figure ($45,183M / $50M = 904x). Net income $10,981M (~$11.0B) stated separately.

claims.statement: Did one no in Dallas kill Blockbuster? Probably not on its own... Would owning Netflix have saved it? Nobody can know.
claims.evidence: Supported by Total Access growth; counterfactual left open; hindsight-fair.

claims.statement: When a small company could replace your core business... Ask what it costs you if it wins.
claims.evidence: One lesson, no factual claim.

notes: Round 4 (remake v2.1): diff check of the five round-3 fixes. All five applied with the exact suggested wording: (1) 900x now on revenue, profit after; (2) Icahn beat reworded to 'Meanwhile... since late two thousand and four', confirmed against the re-opened Schedule 13D (event date 14 Dec 2004, buys from 11 Nov 2004, 5.80%/5.07% at filing, largest holder); (3) 'No store rent'; (4) 'that most retellings skip'; (5) 'In the building: three visitors from California'. No other narration changed versus the round-3 check; all other claims carry over as verified in rounds 1-3 (prospectus, Blockbuster 10-K, FY2006 release, 8-K, Stratrix/Variety/Fortune, Wikipedia, Netflix FY2025 10-K). Quotes: Antioco verbatim and attributed; Randolph framed as memory; Hastings hedged; Apollo 13 and 'dot-com hysteria' omitted. Structure: hook, promise, scene, fairness section, freeze at ~3:15-3:24 of ~8:20 (~40%), reveal, numbers, verdict 'Blockbuster PASSED', one lesson, teaser. ~1,330 words, ~8:20 at speed 1.15 (in range; director should hold beats if the render runs under 8:00). Director notes still binding: no Antioco silhouette at the pitch table; x900 kinetic text on the $45.2B revenue only; Icahn 'late 2004' marker before 'Jan 2005 late fees'. Non-blocking housekeeping for @researcher: mark c33 verified (13D, NBC) with 'stake built from Nov 2004'; c10 date 'prospectus 22 May 2002, delivery 29 May 2002'.
